fichas.title: Operating department and associated facilities
fichas.summary: An operating department comprises theatres and supporting patient and staff control lobbies, preparation and storage areas, waste-disposal facilities, and a nearby recovery room. Patient control includes bed transfer, operating-table preparation, and storage. The department requires replacement power. Equipment preparation for anaesthetic devices separates dirty and clean sides; operating instruments are prepared in the central sterile store outside the operating zone. A plaster room may be provided, especially for departments performing many surgical-orthopaedic operations. Staff lounges should suit department size and provide seating, cupboards, and a sink. Theatre lighting, cleanable surfaces, and controlled ventilation and pressure relationships support operating conditions.
uses: Transfer and prepare patients and operating tables
Prepare anaesthetic devices on separate dirty and clean sides
Prepare operating instruments in a central sterile store
Maintain conditioned, filtered air and pressure control
furniture_equipment: Mobile ceiling-mounted operating light with satellite light

fichas.title: Large operating theatre with associated entry and exit zones
fichas.summary: The illustrated large operating theatre is arranged with associated entry and exit zones. Natural lighting is advantageous psychologically but may be impractical; artificial operating light should reach the work area from directions suited to the incision layout. The theatre should have flat, easily washable floors and walls. Ventilation should avoid uncontrolled air intake, with the operating theatre at the highest pressure and subsidiary and functional rooms at the lowest pressure. Theatre windows should be lockable.
uses: Maintain suitable lighting, hygienic surfaces, and air pressure
